usage_note: Cuban-FL Spanish uses 'panqueque' (singular-leaning) and does NOT use 'hotcakes'. This directly INVERTS the SW dialect — the two Spanish KBs must stay separate.
TRAP: in Cuban-FL usage 'tortilla' means an egg omelette, not a flatbread. Using 'tortilla' for a wrap/flatbread misfires here.
Cafecito: small sweet Cuban espresso, a morning ritual. Accent on the e in café. Strong breakfast-adjacency for Kodiak morning creative.
Colada: shared Cuban espresso served with small cups; a social morning ritual. High cultural-fit signal in Miami-Cuban market.
Breakfast. Shared term, but the ritual (cafecito/colada) is the localization hook.
Cuban toast pressed with butter; a canonical Cuban breakfast bread item.
Blueberries, accent on the a (arándanos). Cuban-FL keeps the standard term rather than 'moras azules'.
Sugar (azúcar), accent on the u. Cafecito is notably sweet — sugar framing lands.
Protein; casual Miami text often drops the accent, standard is proteína.
Child (niño); enye round-trip case for the Cuban file.
Whole-grain 'integral'; shared with SW but re-seeded so this file stands alone.
